key_insight: Streamwise ridges lock and amplify large-scale motions, with ridge height controlling their strength and coexistence with very-large-scale motions, and spacing controlling their location and persistence.
engineering_relevance: Ridge height and spacing offer design levers for controlling large-scale turbulence in open-channel flows, although weak mean secondary motions can mask strong instantaneous activity.
method: Direct numerical simulations of turbulent open-channel flow over streamwise-aligned Gaussian ridges.
Variation of ridge spacing and height.
Proper orthogonal decomposition and conditional averaging of flow structures.
evidence_signal: VLSMs were suppressed at ridge heights h ≥ 0.05δ and re-emerged at h = 0.025δ, while instantaneous secondary motions spanned approximately 2δ and filled the channel height.
watch_item: The reported height thresholds apply to the simulated Gaussian-ridge configurations; transfer to other geometries or flow conditions requires validation.
paper_title: On the relation of secondary motions to large- and very-large-scale motions
